name: Protective conductor mark
summary: A mark on one stroke of a conductor group identifying the protective earth conductor carried with the circuit.
description: This mark identifies the protective conductor within a group of conductors drawn as one line. It shows that the circuit carries its own PE conductor to the load, which is how the fault return path for automatic disconnection is provided in TN systems. The letters PE are often written beside the mark.

The mark does not tell you whether the PE is a separate core, the cable armour or a parallel earth continuity conductor. Each option affects earth fault loop impedance differently, so the cable schedule must say which is used. The mark is also distinct from the protective earth terminal symbol, which shows a connection point rather than a conductor in a run.
readingNotes: Confirm what physically forms the PE: a core, armour or separate conductor.
Check that the PE size meets the protective conductor sizing rule used.
drawingChecklist: Mark the PE on every circuit that carries one.
Identify whether armour is used as the PE.
Show PE terminations at both ends.
distinction: The PE conductor mark identifies a conductor in a run; the protective earth symbol identifies a connection point to the earthing system.
